cover.title: Your invoice is why you're paid *late*
cover.sub: 4 fixes to get paid on the due date.

slides.label: FIX
slides.title: Write a real *due date*
slides.fix: "Payment due by 15 November 2026." A date on the page beats a number of days nobody counts.

slides.label: FIX
slides.title: Take a *deposit* first
slides.fix: 50% before you start, 50% on delivery. Bigger projects: 25 / 50 / 25 by milestone.

slides.label: FIX
slides.title: Agree the *late fee* early
slides.says: A late fee that appears for the first time on an overdue invoice.
slides.fix: Put it in the contract before work starts, then repeat it on every invoice. Same wording, both places.

slides.label: FIX
slides.title: Make paying *easy*
slides.fix: How to pay (bank, UPI or a payment link), the currency, and who to contact. Paying should take 30 seconds.

slides.title: Then a *reminder* rhythm
items: 1 week late: firm note + the agreed fee

items.caption:
Your invoice might be the reason you get paid late. Save this before you send the next one.

1. Write a real due date: "Payment due by 15 November", not just "Net 30"
2. Take a deposit first: 50/50, or 25/50/25 by milestone on bigger projects
3. Agree the late fee in the contract before work starts, then repeat it on every invoice (a fee that first shows up on an overdue invoice rarely sticks)
4. Make paying easy: bank / UPI / payment link, currency, and who to contact

Then follow a reminder rhythm: heads-up 3 days before, re-send on the due date, firm note a week late, pause new work if it's still unpaid.

Not legal advice; check what's standard where you and your client are.

Send this to a freelancer who's still waiting on a payment.

Vague hooks get scrolled. Make yours specific with 3 swaps 👇

1. A number: "some editing tips" → "4 editing cuts"
2. A time: "quickly" → "in 20 minutes"
3. A who: "everyone" → "freelance video editors"

Then the one-read test: if a friend can't repeat your hook after reading it once, cut it again.

Before: "Editing tips"
